label: Incomprehensible: a primitive predicate for being known by no created intellect as fully as knowable
definition: PRIMITIVE. Incomprehensible g: no created intellect knows g as perfectly as g is knowable. After ST I q.12 a.7 (to comprehend is to know a thing as perfectly as it is knowable; God is infinitely knowable and a created intellect knows finitely). Not 'unknowable': a thing can be known truly without being comprehended. Counterexample: a theorem fully understood by a mathematician.
note: Explicitly identified primitive (Encode first). Open semantic obligation: typed created intellects and a measure of knowability. The only constraint placed on it is the open bridge 'Whatever is INFINITE_1 is incomprehensible'.
